data.narrative:
ideaForge is a public-stage drone and autonomous systems company founded by Ankit Mehta, Ashish Bhatt, and Rahul Singh, having raised $50M+. The valuation analysis operates within a constrained peer universe: while five companies populate the Drones & Autonomous sector, the comp set consists of seven private peers including Joby Aviation, Archer Aviation, Zipline, Nuro, and Elroy Air. No public comparables exist in this specific subsector.

The peer-median method is inapplicable here due to insufficient narrow peer clustering. With only two same-stage peers identified and zero adjacent-stage or similar-tier peers meeting screening criteria, the dataset fails to support a robust triangulation at the required minimum threshold of three datapoints. Expanding to an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the structural differences across broader autonomous systems markets. The scarcity of public comps and limited depth of private peer financials constrain traditional multiples-based approaches.

Given these data constraints, a defensible valuation range cannot be established through quantitative triangulation alone. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable public market benchmarks, limited visibility into recent funding rounds among peer private companies, and sector-specific revenue visibility challenges. Further analysis would require either additional transaction-level data from recent private funding events or wait-time for market-driven pricing signals as peer companies approach liquidity events.
